bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographic concentration - all manufacturing facilities are located in Telangana — Flagged in the MD&A as Concentration Risk: regional disruptions such as political instability, natural disasters, regulatory actions or workforce-related challenges could adversely affect operations and logistics. Mitigation is disaster recovery and business continuity measures, regular risk assessments, and expansion into additional geographies being evaluated.
- Raw material dependency and price volatility (stainless steel, nickel alloys, castings) — MD&A Dependency Risk: supply disruptions or price fluctuations may affect operations and profitability; the BRSR separately lists Responsible Supply Chain & Material Sourcing as a risk, noting dependence on critical raw materials and specialised suppliers exposes the Company to supply disruption, price volatility and quality risk. Mitigation is long-term supply arrangements, buffer inventory for critical materials, alternative sourcing, a diversified supplier base and a Supplier Code of Conduct.
- Customer capital-expenditure cycle exposure to macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions — Listed among Threats in the MD&A: economic slowdowns, inflationary pressures, geopolitical tensions and policy instability may adversely impact capital expenditure cycles across key customer industries - the Company sells capital equipment, so demand tracks customer capex.
- Regulatory and statutory compliance risk — MD&A Compliance Risk: operations are subject to environmental, labour and manufacturing regulations, and non-compliance or delays in obtaining statutory approvals could result in penalties, reputational risk or operational disruption. Mitigated through dedicated compliance teams, regular audits, certifications and timely infrastructure upgrades.
- Product quality, warranty and liability risk in critical process applications — MD&A Obligation Risk: product defects or non-conformance to industry specifications could lead to warranty claims, reputational damage, customer dissatisfaction and legal liabilities. Mitigated through stringent quality control across manufacturing units, relevant ISO certifications, warranty provisions in financial planning and customer feedback mechanisms. Product Quality & Customer Satisfaction is also the first material issue in the BRSR, treated there as an opportunity.
- Working capital intensity and interest-rate exposure — MD&A Exposure Risk: working capital requirements and interest rate fluctuations may affect liquidity, finance costs and profitability. Mitigated through diversified banking relationships and continuous monitoring of receivables, inventory cycles and working capital.
- Occupational health and safety in manufacturing operations — The only material issue the BRSR classes as a risk with negative financial implications arising directly from operations: heavy equipment, fabrication processes and hazardous materials expose employees to occupational health and safety risk. Mitigated through an occupational health and safety management system, regular safety training and inspections, PPE and emergency preparedness and incident reporting.
- Business ethics and corporate governance risk — BRSR material issue: failure to maintain high standards of governance and ethical conduct may result in regulatory action, reputational damage and loss of stakeholder confidence. Mitigated through governance policies, a Code of Conduct, a whistle-blower mechanism and periodic compliance reviews under Board oversight.

business.body: The Company designs, engineers, manufactures, installs, commissions and provides lifecycle support for process equipment used by regulated process industries, having evolved from a glass lining equipment manufacturer into a multidisciplinary engineering platform. Its capabilities span glass-lined equipment, process systems, bioprocess solutions, heat transfer equipment, filtration, drying, vacuum technologies and engineering services, delivered to customers across domestic and international markets. In its BRSR the Company reports a single business activity - manufacturing of glass-lined equipment and stainless steel and high alloy equipment, including reactors, receivers, storage tanks, filters, vacuum pumps and allied process equipment, with turnkey solutions primarily for the pharmaceutical and chemical industries - accounting for 100% of turnover.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Build an integrated engineering platform rather than operate as a manufacturer of individual equipment - bringing process engineering, detailed design, precision manufacturing, automation, installation, commissioning and lifecycle support under one organisation so customers engage a single engineering partner across the project lifecycle
- Expand the addressable market beyond traditional glass-lined equipment into turnkey engineering projects across pharmaceuticals, chemicals, biotechnology, food processing and other allied process industries, improving the quality of the revenue mix
- Grow through selective acquisitions and technology collaborations that add complementary capability rather than scale alone - during FY26 the integration of Scigenics and Standard C2C Engineering broadened engineering expertise and strengthened the bioprocess and life-sciences presence
- Run two complementary growth engines: the core process-industry engineering business, and entry into the AI infrastructure ecosystem through a planned investment in GScale Energy covering power and cooling infrastructure for AI data centres
- Drive manufacturing and operational excellence - invest in manufacturing flexibility, throughput, quality systems, automation, digital manufacturing and engineering standardisation across facilities
- Deepen the global technology partnership with GL Hakko Co., Ltd. of Japan in glass-lined process equipment
- Expand the global footprint by strengthening overseas subsidiaries, technology collaborations and regional partnerships to improve market access and diversify the revenue base
- Invest in engineering talent, product development, manufacturing capabilities and technologies to participate in the next generation of industrial growth
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 is described as a defining step in the evolution of the Company's manufacturing capability - a shift from specialised equipment production toward a comprehensive, vertically integrated engineering ecosystem. The expansion came mainly through integration rather than a disclosed greenfield project: the integration of Standard Scigenics extended precision manufacturing into bioprocess, high-purity, biopharmaceutical and life-sciences applications, while the integration of Standard C2C Engineering brought multidisciplinary design and turnkey execution capability (civil, mechanical, electrical and instrumentation scopes) into the platform. These sit alongside sustained investment in manufacturing infrastructure, automation and digital engineering technologies - multi-axis CNC machining centres, automated and robot-assisted welding systems, collaborative robots, coordinate measuring machines, non-destructive testing, real-time production monitoring and data-driven quality control - and a deepened global technology partnership with GL Hakko Co., Ltd. of Japan in glass-lined process equipment. Footprint as stated in the Manufacturing Excellence section: 9+ manufacturing facilities, 180+ engineered product lines and 7 lakhs Sq Ft+ of manufacturing and engineering space; BRSR Section A separately reports 5 plants and 1 office in India and no international plants or offices, and the MD&A notes that all manufacturing facilities are located in Telangana, with expansion into additional geographies being evaluated to reduce location concentration risk. The Company journey timeline records the completion of a new glass lining equipment facility at the SGL Unit and the commencement of operations at Unit 5. Forward expansion is directed at AI data centre infrastructure through power and cooling solutions. No rupee capex quantum, no commissioning dates and no capacity-addition figures are disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Growing demand from process industries - expansion in pharmaceutical, specialty chemical and food & beverage industries is expected to drive demand for high-quality, corrosion-resistant and regulatory-compliant process equipment
- Import substitution and Make in India - focus on domestic manufacturing and government support for localisation create opportunities for Indian manufacturers to replace imported process equipment
- Technology upgradation and digitalisation - adoption of automation, IoT-enabled systems and predictive maintenance offers scope for differentiated, higher-margin products
- Export growth potential - rising demand for cost-effective, quality-assured engineering equipment across Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa
- China +1 manufacturing strategy - supply-chain diversification away from China positions India as an alternative sourcing destination for engineered process equipment
- Benefits from PLI schemes - government Production Linked Incentive schemes for pharmaceuticals and chemicals are expected to support capacity expansion and equipment demand
- Threat: macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty - slowdowns, inflation, geopolitical tension and policy instability may adversely impact capital expenditure cycles across key customer industries
- Threat: raw material price volatility - fluctuations in steel and alloy prices may impact input costs and operating margins
- Margin lever/headwind: employee benefit expenses and other operating costs tied to capability expansion; FY26 employee benefit expenses were 5.61% of revenue from operations

deepdive.thesis: SETL completed its transformation into an integrated turnkey solutions provider with FY26 revenue up 26.7% to INR 793cr, though Q4 margins dipped to 15.5% due to commodity inflation and preemptive hiring. The INR 1,000cr order book and upcoming INR 130cr capex (targeting INR 4,000cr total capacity) position the company for accelerated FY27 growth, leveraging new Japanese tech partnerships and subsidiary synergies.

open.item: To invest INR25-30 crores in capacity for the Shell & Tube Glass Heat Exchanger product (AGI Japan license).
Quarterly revenue run-rate of INR250-300 crores expected from FY27 onwards.
Promoter share pledge (personal purpose) to be removed within ~6 months, possibly earlier.
Shell-and-tube glass-lined heat exchanger unit to come fully into operation July 1, 2026 (200 units/month capacity); ~50 units already made in India Apr-onward, another 50 in hand.
FY26 export revenue doubled vs FY25; expecting continued export growth in FY27 despite war-related discussion delays.
C2C Engineering FY26 revenue INR24cr, targeting INR60cr FY27 (order book ~INR46-47cr); Scigenics ~INR20cr FY26 targeting INR60cr FY27 — ~INR100cr incremental sales.
To invest another INR35-40cr modernising existing plants (robotic/automatic welding & polishing), adding ~30% capacity (util. now ~70-80%).
EBITDA margin (FY26 17.4%, Q4 15.5%) to improve in FY27 via operating leverage and solution-selling; targeted toward ~16-17%+.
FY27 revenue growth to be better than FY26 (which grew 26.7%); can sustain ~25%+ growth.
New 36-acre campus to open entry into oil & gas, nuclear engineering, food & beverage and heavy precision engineering; nuclear/oil&gas entry expected by FY28.
Export contribution targeted at 15%-20% over the next 2 years (25% possible but not assured).
36-acre greenfield project (two phases): INR130cr total (INR65cr this year, INR65cr next); phase-1 50% operational April 1, 2027, phase-2 April 1, 2028; ~INR2,000cr capacity.
Long-term (10-year) objective to reach 40% exports / 60% domestic revenue mix; targeting 30-40% exports in 5-6 years.
Margin pressure flagged from rising commodity/metal input prices and deliberate manpower investment; to be offset via operating leverage and procurement discipline.
New pre-cast buildings subsidiary (Standard Projects) to speed turnkey project delivery (blocks within ~6 months; projects in 12-14 months) for pharma/chemical clients only — not general EPC/civil.
Existing (modernised) facilities to reach ~INR2,000cr capacity and greenfield another ~INR2,000cr, for a combined ~INR4,000 crores revenue capability.
Inorganic growth to continue alongside organic; more acquisitions planned as part of sustainable growth strategy (per new ED Ikeda).
US tariffs (up to ~25-30%) flagged but assessed as ~18-20% cost impact and not materially damaging since products remain cheaper than US manufacturing.
Shell & tube glass heat exchangers expected to add 30%-40% growth to the glass-lining division revenue.
IPO proceeds of INR210 crores: INR130cr working-capital loan repayment (done), INR40cr capex, INR20cr acquisition, balance general corporate.
